what_its_for: This medicine helps your body get rid of ammonia, a harmful waste product that builds up in your blood when your liver cannot process protein properly. It is used to treat a group of rare inherited conditions called urea cycle disorders (UCDs). Without treatment, high ammonia levels can damage your brain and be life-threatening.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with food at the same time each day. It comes as a liquid that you measure carefully with the special dosing syringe provided. You may mix it with a small amount of soft food like applesauce or yogurt, or with a small amount of drink if needed. Swallow it right away and do not save the mixture for later. If you have a feeding tube, your doctor or nurse will show you how to give it that way. Never take more or less than your prescribed dose without talking to your doctor first.
dosing: Your dose is carefully calculated based on your body size and your blood ammonia and amino acid levels. Most adults and children take the medicine spread out over 3 meals each day (morning, midday, and evening). Your doctor will adjust your dose regularly based on blood test results. Always follow exactly what your doctor tells you — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if your next scheduled dose is more than a few hours away. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store the bottle at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). You do not need to refrigerate it, but you may refrigerate it if you prefer. Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep it out of the reach of children. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the bottle. Once opened, use the bottle within 14 days.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating large amounts of protein all at once, as this can raise your ammonia levels quickly. Avoid fasting or skipping meals, as this can also cause ammonia to build up. Do not drink alcohol without first talking to your doctor. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, including probenecid, corticosteroids (like prednisone), and valproic acid, as these can interact with this medicine. Avoid becoming dehydrated — drink plenty of fluids every day.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice any signs of high ammonia (also called hyperammonemia), which can include: unusual sleepiness or extreme tiredness, confusion, memory problems, slurred speech, unsteady walking, unusual behavior or mood changes, vomiting, or seizures. Also contact your doctor if you develop signs of a serious allergic reaction (rash, swelling of face or throat, trouble breathing), or if you have any new or worsening symptoms. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can be dangerous.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working right away to help your body remove excess ammonia. However, finding the right dose may take several weeks and will require regular blood tests. You may not feel any different day to day, but your blood tests will show your doctor how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep all follow-up appointments and never skip doses.
special_populations: Children: This medicine can be used in babies and children as well as adults. Doses are carefully calculated based on body weight and must be measured very precisely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Urea cycle disorders require very careful management during pregnancy, and your doctor will work closely with you. Older adults: Older patients should use this medicine with care and have their blood levels monitored regularly. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver disease, as this may affect how your body handles the medicine.
